compound.name: borneol
compound.one_liner: Bicyclic alcohol related to camphor; in sage and rosemary oils.

occurrences.source_citation: Ghorbani A, Esmaeilizadeh M (2017) Pharmacological properties of Salvia officinalis and its components. J Tradit Complement Med 7(4):433-440
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Ghorbani 2017: 'The main components of the oil include borneol, camphor, caryophyllene, cineole, ...'. EMA lists borneol without a range. | Basis as recorded: ppm as listed by Duke (basis not stated per row; for 'Essent. Oil' parts it is ppm of the oil, 10000 ppm = 1 %)

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Rosmarinus officinalis L., aetheroleum and Rosmarinus officinalis L., folium, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/681037/2021 (29 May 2024). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-rosmarinus-officinalis-l-aetheroleum-rosmarinus-officinalis-l-folium-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: Essential Oil 21000-223000 ppm; Leaf Essent. Oil max 47000 ppm. | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil (Ph. Eur.)

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

compound.teaching_note: Borneol and camphor are an alcohol/ketone pair on the same bornane skeleton.
gaps: No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
